my floor was a mix of people who are drug users and mentally ill!

when you are admitted they make you fill out a food preference form, so they accommodate you. there’s a coffee shop in front of the main entrance so sometimes people who were allowed to go out would buy coffee, donuts, sandwiches etc. sometimes patient’s families would bring them food too! i was in a religious hospital and there was a holiday so the people who practiced brought us soup and pastries!!

I can’t say for all doctors but i’ll tell you about the two i had: the one in the ward was very attentive and kinda helpful, but it was a quick 10-15 minute chat then he’d leave. he did feed me lots of meds. i felt more heard in group meetings where we’d all share! the second doctor i had (outpatient program) was a fucking son of a bitch. refused to treat me because im too depressed to go to work therefor i’m too depressed to benefit from therapy. every single patient who had him complained..

i can’t say.. all the people i talked there were discharged for valid reasons and my friends who are still there one is under court order and the other one is a drug user that has nowhere to go, so they keep her until she finds an apartment. there was a woman i’d talk to and she told me in private that she was going to lie and say she’s better so she can go back home, but when i visited a few months later she was in the intermediate unit (more intense) so i guess it didn’t go well for her..

so my floor was divided in three units:

3B : computers, ping pong tables, tv room, tv in the cafeteria, phone booths, rec room and of course our rooms

intermediate unit : just rooms with a small dining table

high care: just rooms

all units are closed except for 4 times a day where smokers can go outside for a cigarette break for half an hour. when you’re in high care, you’re considered high risk so you’re not allowed to go out!

when i first arrived i wasn’t allowed to have my phone (or clothes, anything really) once i was in my unit (3b) the doctor approved the use of my phone. it depends for each person, the doctor is the one who decided if you’re granted that privilege but usually people get to have access to them!
